text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=api-serving · alert=latency_p99_us-west · severity=critical · link=https://pagerduty.example/alerts/ABC123

alex: Acked. I'm oncall. Starting triage — pulling recent p99/p95 rollups and the us-west autoscaler dashboard.

sara: I see queue depth for the us-west batchers has doubled in the last 2m. p99 jumped from ~320ms -> ~2.1s for short seqs. KV cache hit rate dropped ~15%.

mike: Any recent deploys? I don't see a deploy in last 30m. Could be noisy hotkey or preemptions.

alex: No deploys. Checking node preemptions and GPU memory OOMs. `kubectl get pods -n serving -l region=us-west -o wide` shows a few restarts on sidecar-optimizer.

sara: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-18T02:09:12Z batcher: queue_len=432 p99=2050ms kvcache_hit=72%
2026-03-18T02:09:15Z sidecar: OOMKill pid=2145 reason=OOM
```

mike: OOMs would evict KV cache and push latency up. Propose: 1) temporarily divert traffic for non-enterprise customers to eu-west, 2) scale up us-west batchers, 3) drain problematic nodes.

alex: On it. Starting diversion for low-tier traffic: `redwood route set --from=us-west --to=eu-west --policy=latency-safe --filter=tier!=enterprise` — applying now.

incident-bot: Action triggered: route-change requested by alex · runbook=latency-fanout-v2 · id=route-5689

sara: Scaling up us-west batcher pool by +3 replicas (requested). Also marking the two nodes with restarts as unschedulable.

mike: Good. If KV warmup needed, consider a short cache-warm pass for hot prefixes after nodes stabilize.

alex: Running warmup job: `redwood job run --name=kvcache-warm --targets=us-west-hotkeys --ttl=60s` — job started.

sara: After diversion, observed p99 down to ~900ms for non-enterprise traffic. Enterprise traffic still ~2s. No errors reported (5xx ~unchanged).

mike: That's expected. Keep an eye on autoscaler logs in case of throttling.

alex: I'll stay on until handoff. @jamie — can you take over at 03:30 UTC if this is still active? Summary: cause=us-west sidecar OOM causing KV evictions → elevated p99; mitigations=route diversion for non-enterprise, scale up batchers, kvcache warm job. Customer impact=partial SLO burn for enterprise customers in us-west (~p99 from 350ms→2s). No widespread errors.

jamie: Ack — I'll take it at 03:30 UTC. Bookmarking steps and current links. I'll coordinate with support for customer comms.

alex: @support-bot please prepare a short status draft: impact note + what we're doing. Use priority=customer-facing.

support-bot: Draft created: "We are investigating elevated latency for enterprise customers in US-West. We have diverted some traffic, scaled capacity, and are warming caches. No errors reported. We will update in 30 minutes or sooner." — sending to #support-drafts.

sara: quick check: autoscaler didn't cap out; scaling happened. Remaining action: confirm sidecar OOM root cause in infra and patch it.

alex: Agree. Creating follow-up ticket for infra (link: https://redwood.atlassian/INC-4521). Handoff note added.

jamie: Thanks — I'll monitor metrics and if p99 doesn't improve to <1s for enterprise traffic in 30m I'll escalate PD to infra-oncall. :thumbsup:

alex: Leaving notes and current runbook state. Handing off. :wave:

incident-bot: Thread closed by alex (ack -> resolved-tag pending manual close) · duration=00:23:06
